ctx.x: The University of Indiana has jazz, and Steven was mentioning about North Texas State. They played in some of George Wein's festivals, the number one band, you know, down in Austin, Texas, and those guys sounded like Woody Herman or Maynard Ferguson, a Buddy Rich type band. And just ten of those big twenty-piece jazz bands, all at one time, and the number one band on down, in those days, and I think the University of Nebraska has a big Ashford jazz course, that guy, Alexander, he was up there for awhile, did you…

So all these schools are training a lot of jazz people and then others -- I was just down in Dallas or Houston, a few years ago, to help judge these bands, some school bands. Max Kaminsky was down there, and Jimmy Owens, and quite a few professional players, and they had 30-piece jazz bands. They were using seven trumpets and six trombones,

items.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I can speak about musicians that I have met from the different generations who were very responsible for writing the performance history of this music. I have had interaction with many of them. Teddy Wilson was a beautiful person.

ctx.x: Well, first off, I want to say that I am very proud to have been selected as an NEA Jazz Master. I have been involved with the NEA for many years as a panelist. I can say, I have been on the panel numerous times to select the jazz masters of that year, okay? I recall the panel that selected Art Farmer and Donald Byrd and Herbie Hancock, numerous other people. So, it is really rewarding to think that the panelists and the book that we have with the letters from public people who write in and say, “I think this…

Jazz Masters. Hopefully it is not going to end and I had some words that gave me the feeling that it is not going to end. I hope that is the case. To be recognized by your peers is very, very by your peers. To be recognized by your peers for a situation that you’re not primarily involved with is even more important in my opinion. I have always been a jazz musician, a trumpet player, a composer, arranger, educator, and music consultant. That has been primary for me. Jazz advocacy has been about making life better…
